subject: use INLA as loaded via namespace

messages.author: 9ea95ff2561a8857
messages.subject: use INLA as loaded via namespace
parts:
Hello,
in R, I would like to use INLA as loaded via namespace, that is, not by doing library(INLA), but by doing requireNamespace("INLA"). However I get the following error:

Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : could not find function "inla.models"

Here is a small reproducible example:

requireNamespace("INLA")
data <- as.data.frame(read.table("http://www.math.ntnu.no/inla/r-inla.org/examples/stacks/stacks.dat"))
names(data) = c("y","air","temp","acid")
param.data = list(prec = list(param = c(1.0e-3, 1.0e-3)))
formula1 = y ~ air + temp + acid
mod1 = INLA::inla(formula1, data=data, control.fixed = list(prec = 0.00001), control.family = list(hyper = param.data))

I guess this issue is related to the argument family="gaussian", and the solution may be to use INLA::inla.models(). But I don't directly use inla.models()... So what can I do?

Thanks,
TF

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] use INLA as loaded via namespace
parts:
On Thu, 2016-04-14 at 11:32 -0700, Timothée Flutre wrote:
> Hello,
> in R, I would like to use INLA as loaded via namespace, that is, not
> by doing library(INLA), but by doing requireNamespace("INLA").
> However I get the following error:
>
> Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : could not find function
> "inla.models"

yes. 

what happens doing library(INLA), is that an enviroment is created to
hold the output of inla.models().  see file inlaEnv.R in the repo 

https://bitbucket.org/hrue/r-inla/src/1129969b57eb08fb27ee40bddf364c430
82c53c5/rinla/R/inlaEnv.R?at=default&fileviewer=file-view-default



so you need to create this environment, if it does not exists already,


if (exists(".inlaEnv") && is.environment(.inlaEnv)) {
     ## then reuse it
 } else {
     .inlaEnv = new.env()
 }
 requireNamespace("INLA")




this is impossible to know...

H

--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org

messages.author: e32484f448e128cc
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] use INLA as loaded via namespace
parts:
Hi all,
Not sure whether this has been resolved, but I think we managed to make INLA work with requireNamespace (ie using it as an "Import" from our package) via the following code:
if (!isTRUE(requireNamespace("INLA", quietly = TRUE))) {
      stop("You need to install the packages 'INLA'. Please run in your R terminal:\n install.packages('INLA', repos='https://www.math.ntnu.no/inla/R/stable')")
    }
    # If INLA is installed, then attach the Namespace (so that all the relevant functions are available)
    if (isTRUE(requireNamespace("INLA", quietly = TRUE))) {
      if (!is.element("INLA", (.packages()))) {
        attachNamespace("INLA")
      }
     HERE INCLUDE YOUR CODE
}

HTH
Gianluca
